Rashi on Niddah 26a:10:1.hebrew: הבית טמא - משום אהל המת, דולד הוה בה ומת:
Rashi on Niddah 26a:10:1.english: The house is impure - Because of the tent of the corpse, as there was a fetus in her and it died.

Rashi on Niddah 26a:11:1.hebrew: נימוק הולד - ונעשה דם, ונתערב בדם הלידה, ובטל ברוב:
Rashi on Niddah 26a:11:1.english: The fetus dissolved - And it became blood, and was mixed with the blood of childbirth, and was nullified by the majority.

Rashi on Niddah 26a:12:1.hebrew: וסופה - כשהיא הולכת ורווחת, הויא רחב כתורמוס. לישנא אחרינא: גרסינן בתוספתא: וראשה דומה כתורמוס:
Rashi on Niddah 26a:12:1.english: And its end - As it extends and widens, it is as wide as a lupine. Another version: We read in the Tosefta: "And its head is similar to a lupine."

Rashi on Niddah 26a:14:1.hebrew: שיאחזנו בידו - אחיזה אית בה טפח, שהטפח ארבע אצבעות בגודל:
Rashi on Niddah 26a:14:1.english: That he holds it in his hand - A grasp contains a handbreadth, as a handbreadth is four fingerbreadths [measured] by the thumb.

Rashi on Niddah 26a:15:1.hebrew: שדרו של לולב צריך שיהא יוצא מן ההדס טפח - לבד אורך העלין. שדרה קרי כל זמן שהעלין הולכין ומתחברין ומוסיפין, ואחר שכלתה השדרה, גבוהין אורך העלין למעלה:
Rashi on Niddah 26a:15:1.english: The spine of a lulav must protrude a handbreadth beyond the myrtle - [This is] exclusive of the length of the leaves. It is called the "spine" as long as the leaves continue to attach and be added [to it], and after the spine ends, the length of the leaves extends high above.

Rashi on Niddah 26a:16:1.english: It is [only] one - For there is no Amoraic statement other than this [one] regarding the spine, which Rabbi Yoḥanan said.

Rashi on Niddah 26a:16:2.hebrew: אמר אביי - לא תימא: תני ר' חייא אזוב טפח, דמשמע מתני' היא; אלא אימא: אמר רבי חייא, ומנפשיה קאמרה. ורבי חייא תנא ואמורא הוא, והיכא דאמר מנפשיה בלשון מימרא, הויא שמעתא:
Rashi on Niddah 26a:16:2.english: Abaye said - Do not say: "Rabbi Ḥiyya taught: Hyssop is a handbreadth," which implies that it is a Tannaitic teaching; rather, say: "Rabbi Ḥiyya said," and he stated it of his own accord. And Rabbi Ḥiyya was a Tanna and an Amora, and when he spoke of his own accord in the phrasing of an Amoraic statement, it is an Amoraic tradition.

Rashi on Niddah 26a:17:1.english: A handbreadth by a handbreadth with a height of a handbreadth - A small tent that is a handbreadth in length and a handbreadth in width, and the height of its interior space is a handbreadth.

Rashi on Niddah 26a:17:2.hebrew: מביא הטומאה - אם כזית מן המת בצד זה וכלי בצד זה, הוה טמא כלי מחמת אהל המת:
Rashi on Niddah 26a:17:2.english: Transmits the impurity - If an olive-bulk of a corpse is on this side and a vessel is on that side, the vessel becomes impure due to the tent of the corpse.

Rashi on Niddah 26a:17:3.hebrew: וחוצץ בפני הטומאה - אם טומאה תחתיו וכלי על גביו, הכלי טהור. ולהכי נקט על רום טפח, דאי הוה חלל רומו פחות מטפח, הויא טומאה רצוצה, וכנגדו למעלה עד לרקיע טמא, כדאמרי' בהעור והרוטב (חולין קכו.). ולענין אתויי טומאה נמי לא מייתי, דלאו אהל הוא:
Rashi on Niddah 26a:17:3.english: And serves as a barrier before the impurity - If impurity is beneath it and a vessel is on top of it, the vessel is pure. And that is why [the mishna] specified "with a height of a handbreadth," for if the height of its interior space were less than a handbreadth, it would be compressed impurity, and [whatever is] opposite it upward up to the sky is impure, as we say in [the chapter] "HaOr VeHaRotev" (Chullin 126a). And with regard to transmitting impurity as well, it does not transmit, as it is not a tent.

Rashi on Niddah 26a:19:1.hebrew: תנור - מקום שפיתת שתי קדרות. כירה - מקום שפיתת קדרה אחת:
Rashi on Niddah 26a:19:1.english: An oven - A place for setting two pots. A stove is a place for setting one pot.

Rashi on Niddah 26a:19:2.hebrew: חבור - וכתנור דמי, מפני שצריכה לתנור להיות לו יד, שאם נטמא התנור, פת שעליה טמא. שהתנור, אע"פ שאינו מקבל טומאה מגבו, מטמא הוא את אחרים מגבו, כדאמר בתורת כהנים. הלכך ידו, אע"ג דלית ליה אויר, מטמא. אבל יותר מטפח עומדת לינטל, שהיא גדולה יותר מדאי, ולא הויא יד:
Rashi on Niddah 26a:19:2.english: A connection - And it is considered like the oven, because it is needed for the oven to serve as a handle for it, so that if the oven becomes impure, bread that is upon it is impure. For an oven, even though it does not contract impurity from its exterior, transmits impurity to other items from its exterior, as stated in Torat Kohanim. Therefore, its handle, even though it has no airspace, transmits impurity. However, [if it protrudes] more than a handbreadth, it is slated to be removed, as it is excessively large, and does not constitute a handle.

Rashi on Niddah 26a:1:1.hebrew: גבי בכורות - דקתני (בכורות דף מו.): המפלת סנדל, הבא אחריו בכור לנחלה, ואין בכור לכהן:
Rashi on Niddah 26a:1:1.english: With regard to firstborns - As [the mishna] teaches (Bekhorot 46a): "One who miscarries a sandal, that which comes after it is a firstborn for inheritance, but is not a firstborn for a priest."

Rashi on Niddah 26a:1:2.hebrew: למאי הלכתא - קס"ד לבא אחריו לסוף שנה או לסוף שנתיים קמיירי, ול"ל סנדל? והלא בלא סנדל פטר ולד דבהדיה את הבא אחריו! ומשני: לבא אחריו. כלומר, לכך הוזכר סנדל: אם יצא ולד שעמו אחריו, הוי בכור לנחלה ולא בכור לכהן:
Rashi on Niddah 26a:1:2.english: For what halakha - [The Gemara] initially thought that [the mishna] is dealing with [a child] who comes after it at the end of a year or at the end of two years, and why do I need [the mishna to mention] a sandal? For even without a sandal, the child that was with it would exempt the one that comes after it! And [the Gemara] answers: [It refers] to the one that comes after it. That is to say, this is why a sandal was mentioned: If the child that was with it emerged after it, he is a firstborn for inheritance, but not a firstborn for a priest.

Rashi on Niddah 26a:3:1.english: With regard to Keritot - In the first chapter (Keritot 7b), regarding the obligation of a sacrifice.

Rashi on Niddah 26a:3:2.hebrew: למאי הלכתא - תיפוק ליה, דמשום ולד שעמו תביא קרבן:
Rashi on Niddah 26a:3:2.english: For what halakha - Let it be derived [from elsewhere], for on account of the offspring that is with it she must bring an offering.

Rashi on Niddah 26a:4:1.hebrew: ולד יוצא דרך דופן - ע"י סם, לא מיחייבה קרבן, דכתיב גבי קרבן (ויקרא יב) אשה כי תזריע וילדה זכר, עד שתלד ממקום שמזרעת:
Rashi on Niddah 26a:4:1.english: An offspring that emerges via Caesarean section - [Delivered] by means of a drug, she is not obligated [to bring] an offering, as it is written regarding the offering (Leviticus 12:2): "If a woman conceives and gives birth to a male" — [she is not obligated] until she gives birth from the place where she conceives.

Rashi on Niddah 26a:5:1.english: And according to Rabbi Shimon, etc. - [This is stated] later, in the chapter "Yotzei Dofen" (Niddah 40a).

Rashi on Niddah 26a:7:1.english: When they emerge - The sandal [fetus] and the offspring with it.

Rashi on Niddah 26a:7:2.hebrew: כרוכין - דבוקין זה בזה, ולא דבוקין ממש. ומדיוצאין יחד, אי אפשר שתתגייר בינתיים:
Rashi on Niddah 26a:7:2.english: Wrapped - Attached to one another, but not literally attached. And since they emerge together, it is impossible for her to convert in the interim.

Rashi on Niddah 26a:8:1.hebrew: שמע מינה - מדהוזכר סנדל גבי כריתות משום גירות, וכגון שיצא ולד תחלה ואחר כן סנדל, וגבי בכורות כגון שיצא סנדל תחלה, כדאוקמינן לעיל דפוטר ולד מחמש סלעים, ותניא דבבת אחת יוצאין — שמע מינה: אין שוכבין זה אצל זה, דא"כ לא משכחת לה שיצא זה קודם זה. אלא האי כרוכין דקתני, הכי הוא: מכרך כריך ליה ולד לסנדל אפלגיה, דראש הולד תחוב כנגד טיבורו של סנדל:
Rashi on Niddah 26a:8:1.english: Conclude from it - Since a sandal was mentioned with regard to Keritot on account of conversion, and [namely in a case] where the [viable] offspring emerged first and afterward the sandal; and with regard to Bekhorot [in a case] where the sandal emerged first, as we established above, that it exempts the [viable] offspring from five selaim; and [yet] it is taught that they emerge at the same time — conclude from it: they do not lie next to each other, for if so, you would not find [it possible] that this one emerged before that one. Rather, this [term] "wrapped" that is taught means this: the offspring wraps around the sandal at its midpoint, as the head of the offspring is inserted opposite the navel of the sandal.

Rashi on Niddah 26a:8:2.hebrew: ומשלחיף ליה כלפי רישיה - כלומר, דחפו ולד בראשו לסנדל כלפי חוץ:
Rashi on Niddah 26a:8:2.english: And pushes it toward its head - That is to say, the offspring pushed the sandal with its head toward the outside.

Rashi on Niddah 26a:8:3.hebrew: גבי בכורות - דבעינן שיצא הסנדל תחילה, כגון שיצאו דרך ראשיהן כו':
Rashi on Niddah 26a:8:3.english: Regarding firstborns - Since we require that the sandal [fetus] emerge first, [this is] for example where they emerged headfirst, etc.

Rashi on Niddah 26a:9:1.english: Directly adjacent - Lying next to each other.

Rashi on Niddah 26a:9:2.hebrew: ואיפוך שמעתתא - מימרא דרב פפא, דאמר בבכורות שיצאו דרך ראשיהן:
Rashi on Niddah 26a:9:2.english: And reverse the teaching - The statement of Rav Pappa, who said that in *Bekhorot* they emerged via their heads.

Rashi on Niddah 26a:9:3.hebrew: סריך - אוחז בידיו למעלה ואינו ממהר לצאת, וסנדל מחליק ויוצא קודם:
Rashi on Niddah 26a:9:3.english: Hangs on - It holds on with its hands above and does not hurry to emerge, and the sandal [fetus] slides and emerges first.

Rashi on Niddah 26a:9:5.hebrew: הויא לידה - דקיימא לן בהאי פירקא (דף כח.): יצא ראשו, הרי הוא כילוד. אבל סנדל, עד דנפיק רובא, דאין ראש נפל חשוב, דהכי אמרינן בבכורות (דף מו:): אין הראש פוטר בנפלים. ואדנפיק סנדל, נתגיירה וטבלה:
Rashi on Niddah 26a:9:5.english: It is a birth - For we maintain in this chapter (page 28a): [Once] its head has emerged, it is considered born. But [in the case of] a sandal [fetus, it is not considered born] until the majority [of its body] has emerged, as the head of a non-viable fetus is not considered significant; for so we say in Bekhorot (page 46b): "The [emergence of the] head does not exempt in [the case of] non-viable fetuses." And while the sandal was emerging, she converted and immersed.

Tosafot on Niddah 26a:13:1.hebrew: שדרה טפח - וא"ת, תקשי הך ברייתא לרב יהודה אמר שמואל, דאמר: צריך שיצא לולב מן ההדס טפח, ולא מצריך שדרה, ופליג על ר' פרנך? וי"ל, דלא מתניא בי ר' חייא ובי ר' אושעיא. אי נמי, בברייתא לא תני שדרה, אלא שהש"ס קבע בברייתא שדרה משום דקים לן הכי. ואם תאמר, דטפח זה קטן, דמפרש התם: אמה בת ה' טפחים עשה אותה בת ו', צא מהם ג' להדס ואחד ללולב? ויש לומר, דמכל מקום כיון דאיכא שם טפח עליה, חשיב ליה הכא עם שאר טפחים. אי נמי, טפח דלולב לא קאי אטפחים קטנים, ולא קאי קטנים כ"א אטפחים של הדס:
Tosafot on Niddah 26a:13:1.english: The spine [measures] a handbreadth - And if you say: Let this baraita pose a difficulty to Rav Yehuda [who] said [in the name of] Shmuel, who said that the lulav must emerge from the myrtle branch by a handbreadth, and does not require the spine [specifically], and disagrees with Rabbi Parnakh? And one can say that it was not taught in the academy of Rabbi Ḥiyya and in the academy of Rabbi Oshaya. Alternatively, in the baraita it did not teach "spine"; rather, the Talmud established [the wording] "spine" in the baraita because this is established for us [as the halakha]. And if you say that this handbreadth is a small one, as it explains there [in Sukkah 32b]: "A cubit of five handbreadths, make it into six; take from them three for the myrtle branch and one for the lulav"? And one can say: In any case, since the name "handbreadth" applies to it, it counts it here along with the other handbreadths. Alternatively, the [extra] handbreadth of the lulav does not refer to small handbreadths, and [the calculation of] small [handbreadths] applies only to the handbreadths of the myrtle branch.

Tosafot on Niddah 26a:17:1.hebrew: ותו ליכא - ואם תאמר: והא איתא בהמוכר את הספינה (ב"ב דף פט.) קנה של מאזנים טפח, ובהעור והרוטב (חולין דף קכג.) בכדי אחיזה טפח, גם בטרפות יש דשיעורו טפח? ולפי המסקנא דלא איירי בדרבנן, אלא בדכתיב ולא מפורש שיעורייהו, אתי שפיר:
Tosafot on Niddah 26a:17:1.english: And are there no more - And if you say: But behold, it is [stated] in [the chapter] HaMokher Et HaSefina (Bava Batra 89a) [that] the beam of a balance scale [is] a handbreadth, and in [the chapter] HaOr VeHaRotev (Chullin 123a) [that] an amount sufficient for grasping [is] a handbreadth, [and] also in [the laws of] tereifot there is [a defect] whose measure is a handbreadth? [Yet] according to the conclusion [of the Gemara], that [he] does not deal with Rabbinic [laws], but rather with [matters] that are written [in the Torah] and their measurements are not specified, it works out well.

Tosafot on Niddah 26a:19:1.hebrew: מן התנור טפח - היינו להוציא הטומאה, שאם נטמא התנור מתוכו, נטמא היד, דחשיב כגוף התנור. דאף על גב דאין התנור מקבל טומאה מגבו, אם נטמא תוכו, גבו נמי טמא, כדאמר פ' אלו דברים (ברכות דף נב:), דנטמא תוכו כולן טמאין. ובת"כ נמי אמר: מרובה מדת לטמא ממדת ליטמא, שמטמא אחרים מגבו ואינו מיטמא מגבו. ויד דין גב יש לה; ואם נגע השרץ ליד, לא נטמא התנור, כדאמרינן בתוספתא (ב"ק דכלים פ"ו): אין טומאה לכלי חרס אלא מתוכו והיסטו בלבד, ולא קתני על ידו. ובהעור והרוטב (חולין דף קיח.), דבעי למימר יד להכניס, יעמיד התוספתא בתנור שאין לו יד:
Tosafot on Niddah 26a:19:1.english: [Protruding] from the oven, a handbreadth - This means [that it functions as a handle only] to transmit impurity [outward]: for if the oven became defiled from its interior, the handle becomes defiled, as it is considered like the body of the oven. For although an oven does not contract impurity from its back [i.e., its exterior], if its interior became defiled, its back is also defiled, as [the Gemara] states in the chapter [entitled] "Elu Devarim" (Berakhot 52b), that if its interior became defiled, all of them [i.e., all parts of the vessel] are defiled. And in Torat Kohanim it also states: "The measure to transmit impurity is greater than the measure to contract impurity, for it defiles other [objects] from its back, but it does not contract impurity from its back." And a handle has the status of the back [of the oven]; thus, if a creeping animal touched the handle, the oven does not become defiled, as we say in the Tosefta (Bava Kamma of Kelim, ch. 6): "There is no impurity for an earthenware vessel except from its interior and [through] its being shifted (hesto) alone," and it does not teach "[or through] its handle." And in [the chapter entitled] "HaOr VehaRotev" (Chullin 118a), which seeks to say that there is a handle to bring in [impurity], it will establish the Tosefta as [referring to] an oven that does not have a handle.

Tosafot on Niddah 26a:3:1.hebrew: סנדל - דלית ליה חיותא עד שיצא רובו, אבל ראשו לא. אע"ג דשמואל, דאמר אין הראש פוטר בנפלים, איתותב בפ' יש בכור (בכורות דף מו:), נפל דאית ליה צורת פנים עדיף מסנדל. והא דקאמר ולד דאית ליה חיותא מדנפיק רישיה, לאו דוקא דאית ביה חיותא, דהא אפי' לית ביה חיותא, כיון דאיתותב שמואל; ועוד, דמשמע בירושלמי דולד שעם הסנדל אינו מתקיים; אלא כלומר, שראוי לחיות, דהיינו שנגמר בצורת פנים. ור"ח גריס: ולד דאית ביה חיותא מדנפיק רובי', סנדל דלית ביה חיותא מדנפיק כוליה. פי': רוביה — רוב הראש, כוליה — כל הראש; אבל כל הגוף, פשיטא דלא צריך, דרובו ככולו:
Tosafot on Niddah 26a:3:1.english: A sandal - [Since] it has no vitality, [it is not considered born] until most of it emerges, but [the emergence of] its head is not [sufficient]. Even though Shmuel, who said that the head does not exempt in [the case of] non-viable fetuses (nefalim), was refuted in the chapter [entitled] "Yesh Bekhor" (Bekhorot 46b) — a non-viable fetus that has the form of a face (tzurat panim) is superior to a sandal. And that which [the Gemara] says: "A fetus that has vitality, once its head emerges [it is considered born]" — [this is] not strictly [meaning] that it has vitality (i.e., is viable), for even [if] it does not have vitality [its head suffices], since Shmuel was refuted; and furthermore, for it is implied in the Yerushalmi that the fetus that is with the sandal does not survive; rather, [the Gemara means] as if to say: that it is fit to live, that is, that it was completed with the form of a face. And Rabbeinu Chananel (R"Ch) read: "A fetus that has vitality, once its majority emerges; a sandal, which does not have vitality, once all of it emerges." He explained: "Its majority" [means] the majority of the head; "all of it" [means] the entire head. But [as for] the entire body, it is obvious that it is not required, as the majority of it is like all of it.
